summary:
SPHEREx Explorer is a project designed to make NASA's SPHEREx data easier to access and explore. It consists of a proof-of-concept web application for searching, visualising, and comparing astronomical observations, alongside Python tools intended to simplify programmatic access to the archive. By combining these capabilities, the project aims to make SPHEREx data more accessible to students, researchers, and developers, while providing a foundation for building further applications using real astronomical observations.

IRSA can be the victim of a DDoS attack, during which operations may temporarily suspend and requests may fail.
details:
Overview:

The SPHEREx Explorer is a web application used to easily visualise and explore the data provided by NASA's SPHEREx space telescope.

SPHEREx provides data from scanning the whole sky across 102 near-infrared wavelengths. This can be used to understand our universe better. However, it can be complex to understand and explore different data products due to needing to use astronomical archives, specific file types and science software.

This project has created an interactive tool which allows users to input coordinates in Right Ascension and Declination. A radius can then be entered to search for observations within that area. It can download and display FITS images for users to analyse such as IMAGE, FLAGS, VARIANCE and ZODI.

Features such as sky navigation and observation comparison have been included in this prototype. Observations can be compared together by aligning them using their World Coordinate System. A difference map can be created to compare two observations. This shows any unusual pixels that can be investigated further. These aren’t actual discoveries but are just candidates.

The aim of this project was to increase the ease of exploring SPHEREx data. By using this application users can carry out some of the tasks required to explore the data rather than having to do it manually. This could encourage students, teachers, developers and researchers to explore the data as it is much easier to understand.

The project was mainly created using Python. Streamlit was used to create the interactive web application. Astroquery was used to interact with the IRSA archive. Astropy was used to work with astronomical coordinates, FITS files and World Coordinate System. Other packages used were NumPy and Pandas to process data, Matplotlib to visualise data, Requests to obtain data products and SciPy to align and process images. The application was deployed using Streamlit Community Cloud.

The creativity behind this project is that the search, FITS analysis, sky navigation and observation comparison was all put into one easy to use application. We wanted to ensure users were actually interacting with real data from the mission rather than just creating another visualisation.

Factors such as ease of use, public data, large astronomical files, accurate coordinates and accurate comparisons were all considered.

Alongside the web application, we have developed a reusable Python library for accessing SPHEREx data. It aims to simplify common tasks involved in searching the archive and retrieving astronomical data products, allowing other developers to integrate SPHEREx data into their own applications. This library and the web application provide two different ways to explore and work with the mission's public data.

Use of SI tools: ChatGPT and GitHub Copilot were used during development to assist with coding, debugging, troubleshooting, and editing written documentation. The team reviewed and tested the resulting code and made project decisions and implementation changes themselves.
